literal_cells: 2334 / EP839 finite subsidiary question (current EP867): Erdős1992, Some forgotten problems, printedp43 — can a consecutive-sum-avoiding subset of[1,N] exceed N/2+O(1)?

Róbert Freud, Adding Numbers, James Cook Mathematical Notes6, issue60(January1993),6199–6202. Existing published finite negative answer, not a new discovery or upload from this sweep. For every integer y>=1, the inspected four-block construction gives an increasing admissible set F_y in[1,144y-12] with76y-7 elements and excess4y-1 above half. Admissible means no term is a sum of two or more consecutive earlier terms. This unbounded excess refutes every additive-constant half ceiling; the same finite sets imply the uniform lower bound f(N)>=19N/36-77. Full four-page note and complete finite proof independently checked; current institutional issue PDF is https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/cook/iss_no60.PDF . No DOI for Freud's note was authenticated, so this DOI cell is intentionally empty. This covers only the separate finite clause, not EP839's infinite lower-natural-density or logarithmic-density questions. Coppersmith–Phillips1996, DOI10.1137/S0895480193244139, is a distinct stronger published13/24 claim whose identity/abstract were verified but whose full proof remains inaccessible; its DOI is not Freud's DOI and is not certified here as a checked13/24 proof.
